goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: The merged baseline already provides cue ownership, atomic lifecycle/history, shared editor/CLI dispatch, compiler-native preview, trajectory controls, and canvas-first disclosure. Type, Select, Drag, and reusable Hold are absent; the existing hold is fixture-locked. The architecture fully orders this as the next vertical slice. One end-to-end Worker package is the largest safe unit, provided it preserves existing cue bytes, introduces no alternate runtime, and uses synthetic fixtures until ignored private locks are available. Parallel writing is unsafe because all four cues intersect the same domain, protocol, service, CLI, and editor dispatch surfaces.
evidence: Baseline: local origin/main resolves to df0075b4932455118a094993c6c9401b6a02fff0; merged PRs #9, #10, and #11 are present as fdea49a, 55ed967, and df0075b.

Capability matrix — Type: no canonical semantic, protocol schema, CLI parser, editor workflow, generator bundle, or browser proof exists. Existing step-timed CSS support is reusable infrastructure only.

Capability matrix — Select: no canonical semantic or workflow exists. Existing cursor/click primitives provide target identity and press feedback but do not model approach/choose/settle or optional highlight ownership.

Capability matrix — Drag: stable trajectory/moment operations and canvas handles exist, but there is no cue-owned coordinated cursor-plus-dragged-target semantic, endpoint contract, CLI parity, or cue proof.

Capability matrix — Hold: motion.hold.insert and motion.settled-hold.set are fixed to one synthetic cue/boundary and 600 ms. Generic cue replacement, detach, and exact inverse machinery exists, but reusable scoped hold expansion does not.

Semantic decision: preserve motion.cursor-click-reveal generator version 1 and its existing derived IDs/bytes. Dispatch the four new kinds through a separately versioned generator; never reinterpret or migrate existing attached cues implicitly.

Semantic decision: Type targets one existing text element and materializes width reveal from 0% to 100% with steps(stepCount,end), fill both, and no copy or DOM creation. Every step boundary is proof-addressable.

Semantic decision: Select uses approach < choose < settle. The generator gives the existing cursor a deterministic press response; an optional existing highlight gains visibility/opacity at choose and remains selected. Without a highlight, the selected element receives a deterministic visual pulse. Constants belong to the generator version, not hidden document state.

Semantic decision: Drag stores explicit stage-normalized dragged-object waypoints plus a fixed cursor grab offset. The cursor approaches the first grip point, cursor and object move together from move-start through arrive, and both retain the endpoint through release. Ordering is approach < press <= move-start < arrive < release.

Semantic decision: Hold requires exitMs = enterMs + durationMs, an ordered stable target/track scope, and a digest-checked replacement bundle. Each affected track must have an explicit value boundary at enter or creation fails closed; expansion duplicates that boundary at exit and shifts later affected timing. Delete restores source; detach preserves generated bytes.

Private availability: five HTML scene inputs are locally available. No adjacent stylesheet or font assets were observed, and this checkout has no ignored private-acceptance directory. Private proof therefore requires out-of-band digest-locked font/materialization inputs in the new worktree; public synthetic implementation may proceed without them.

Worktree prerequisite: create the isolated branch from df0075b4932455118a094993c6c9401b6a02fff0, not the behind/dirty main checkout; transfer only this goal's control files and never private corpus bytes.

Chrome proof: on a named localhost subdomain, author all four cues from the canvas, edit their principal moments/geometry, persist and reload, reproduce equivalent operations through CLI/service, and observe only compiler-created browser animations with zero console, page, request, or unexpected-network errors.

Boundary proof: sample Type at every step boundary t-1/t/t+1; Select at choose and settle; Drag at press, move-start, arrive, and release; Hold at enter and exit. Repeat export/proof runs, verify equal digests, inspect reduced motion, and exercise keyboard order plus narrow/wide layouts.
Adversarial failures to falsify: cue/track authority or detach/history drift; editor/CLI divergence or partial durable writes; preview/proof using a second runtime or leaking private material.

Current verification entry points on origin/main include test:unit, test:phase3:service, test:phase3:recovery, test:phase3:parity, test:phase3:browser, test:browser, qa:chrome, test:visual, test:visual:authoring, test:visual:trajectory, verify:determinism, typecheck, build, check:sensitive, check:private-ignore, and git diff --check.

parallel_safety.reason: All four cue kinds share the cue union, generator dispatch, validation, operation preparation, protocol schema, CLI parser, durable service path, and unified editor workflow; disjoint write ownership cannot be proven.
